title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for Real estate portfolio management
audience: Portfolio management businesses in any service business who want repeat appointments and referrals from owners they already manage for, and from owners who have sold or handed over property.
learningOutcomes: Plan a review or referral request that is made after the owner confirms the result, and that the owner can decline easily.
Write a next-service offer for portfolio work with a date, a scope and a fee approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it.
Write referral reward terms, including the payment condition, before any referral is made.

instruction.heading: Ask at the moment the owner is most satisfied
instruction.body: The best time to ask for a review or referral is after the owner has confirmed the result is right, usually at the end of a first full statement cycle, after a tenancy handover that went well, or when an invoice is paid. Ask in one sentence, name the step you would like, such as a review or the name of one owner who might need management, and make it easy to decline. Timing matters. In one Baylor Keller Center experiment, a late reminder brought in more reviews than an immediate one: 1.32 per cent of customers left a review with no reminder, against 2.16 per cent with a late reminder. That is one experiment only, and it was not run on property management. Sending a review link or QR code is allowed, and Google provides one. Do not write reviews for owners or tenants, and do not invent them. Do not screen out unhappy owners so that complaints stay hidden. Podium, a review-software vendor, says Google treats asking only happy customers as a violation, and that position was not checked against Google's own policy. The ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews, including for changing or removing negative reviews.

instruction.heading: Offer the next service before the owner leaves
instruction.body: Repeat work is the core of a portfolio business. At the end of each cycle, propose the next step with a date: a property inspection at a set interval, a lease renewal review before the expiry date, a planned maintenance programme for the year, or a management review of a property the owner is adding. Put the proposed scope, the interval and the fee approach in writing, and confirm that the owner agrees before you change their appointment. A written next step turns a passing comment into continuing work. If the written offer goes by email or text, check the electronic message rules first. ACMA's guidance indicates that inferred consent is narrow and does not cover a message sent just after a purchase. No source read for this course gives a repeat-work pattern or retention figure for portfolio management, so the interval must be tested in your own records.

instruction.heading: Check in at the interval that suits the work
instruction.body: Schedule a check-in after a period that suits the work. For a managed property, a suggested starting point of about ninety days is a choice to test, not a benchmark, and the check may follow each seasonal inspection. The check asks whether the arrangement still suits the owner, whether anything has changed, and whether there is other work to quote. Keep it short, record the reply and close the loop. A check-in that only asks about the service may not be commercial, but a message that promotes any service can be, even when it is framed as a reminder (Clayton Utz, ACMA enforcement, 9 November 2023). ACMA's summary does not say whether one-to-one messages are covered, so check that point before you send.

instruction.heading: Re-contact previous owners before their busy periods
instruction.body: Portfolio work follows the calendar and the lease cycle: lease expiries, end-of-financial-year reporting, pre-sale reviews, and spring inspections. Plan a short message a few weeks before each one. Offer the slots you can deliver, on written terms, with a clear way to opt out. Do not use the message to pressure anyone, and do not contact an owner who has asked not to hear from you. ACMA's guidance says an unsubscribe must be honoured within five working days, so record each opt-out as soon as you receive it and stop sending to that owner. At the end of each period, review the response and note which timing worked. Do not use tenants' personal details for marketing.

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: A referral reward works best when the owner knows the terms before they refer someone. Decide what you will offer, such as a credit on the next management invoice or a small thank-you, and write down the payment condition, which is normally that the referred owner has signed an appointment. Give the referrer a copy of the terms. A study of referral programmes found that stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referrals across seven studies, so say what the reward is in the invitation (Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research, 2023; no figures used here). Get the referred person's consent before any referral message is sent. An older Clayton Utz article (2017) makes the same point about consent. Check any cash-based reward, and its tax or contract effect, and any licence rule that applies to the referred work, with an adviser. No business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found, so those points remain unconfirmed. Do not pay a reward that depends on the terms of a tenancy outcome without checking the trust and commission rules first.

procedure: After each cycle is signed off with the owner, make one review or referral request and record what was asked and the answer.
Write the next-service offer with a date, scope, interval and fee approach, and confirm it with the owner.
Schedule the check-in for the interval that suits the work, and send it using the electronic message rules.
Plan a re-contact message for each busy period in the calendar, and exclude anyone who has opted out.
Write the referral reward terms and the payment condition before the first referral is made.
When a referral signs an appointment, confirm the reward condition is met before applying the reward, and record the outcome.
Review at the end of each year which requests, offers and timings produced repeat work.

workedExamples.situation: A manager looks after three units for a landlord. The landlord says he will recommend the manager to a neighbour who owns two units, and suggests a credit on his own next management invoice if the neighbour signs an appointment.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the manager do before the neighbour signs, and what should she avoid?
workedExamples.reasoning: She writes the reward terms before any referral happens: the credit on the landlord's next invoice, the condition that the neighbour signs an appointment and the first statement cycle is complete, and when the credit is applied. She asks the landlord to pass on the neighbour's details, and contacts the neighbour only if the neighbour agrees. She does not promise a reward she has not written down, and she does not publish the landlord's name, the tenants' names or the property address in a review without consent for that use. Because a credit that reduces a fee may affect commission and trust rules, she checks those rules and confirms the tax and contract effect with an adviser. She accepts only work that her licence covers in the state where the property is.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the cycle sign-off date and the review or referral request made
Next-service offer template with scope, interval and fee approach
Calendar of seasonal re-contact dates for portfolio work
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any site visit follows the site's own safety rules

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the owner has confirmed the result.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask after the cycle is signed off or the invoice is paid, when the owner has confirmed the result is right.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral reward that was never written down, so the terms are disputed later.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral is made, and give the referrer a copy.

commonErrors.error: Publishing an owner's, tenant's or property's details without consent for that use.
commonErrors.prevention: Get consent for each thing you plan to publish, and keep the record. Never use tenants' personal details for marketing.

commonErrors.error: Contacting an owner who asked not to hear from you, or using a re-contact message to pressure them.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list, honour it at once, and keep re-contact messages factual and optional.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing an owner's, tenant's or property's details needs the person's consent for that use. Do not write reviews on a client's behalf or invent them. If the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies to your business, client and tenant details are personal information. Whether the Act applies to a small business depends on its turnover and other factors, and that point is unconfirmed here, so check the OAIC guidance.

Review platforms and referral programmes can have their own rules on incentives. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews. The ACCC's guidance on online reviews says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on the review's content. Check each platform's rules before offering any reward.

Check-in and re-contact messages sent by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). A message that promotes any service can be commercial even when it is framed as a service reminder, and ACMA has been enforcing this area, so check each message before sending.

A referral does not extend the licence or authority of the business that accepts the work. Accept only work that your licence covers, in the state where the property is. In Queensland, real estate agent and resident letting agent licences cover letting property and collecting rent for others for reward (Property Occupations Act 2014, sections 26 and 27; excerpt read only). This lesson does not grant any licence.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after sign-off or payment, and includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-service offer is written, has a date and is confirmed by the owner before the appointment changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log with the date sent and the answer.
Next-service offers with the date, scope, interval and owner confirmation.
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome.
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after the owner has confirmed the result, and make it easy to say no.
Offer the next portfolio step in writing, with a date, before the owner leaves.
Set referral rewards and their payment conditions in writing before anyone refers.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask an owner for a review or referral?
options: Before the appointment is signed, so the owner feels committed
After the owner has confirmed the result is right
Only when the owner has sent you a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: An owner wants to publish a review with their name and the address of a managed property. What do you need?
options: Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own judgement that the address is already public
The owner's consent for the name and address you plan to publish

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred owner signs, based on how keen the referrer seems
Decided and written in advance, with the condition for payment stated

knowledgeChecks.question: When does the lesson say to propose the next step for the owner?
options: At the end of each cycle, with a date

officialReferences.title: Avoid sending spam (ACMA)
officialReferences.covers: Says commercial messages need the recipient's consent, must identify the sender, and must carry an unsubscribe option that works for at least 30 days and is honoured within five working days. Does not mention one-to-one messages. Read in the CP-04 research on 2026-11-09.

officialReferences.title: Online reviews for product and services (ACCC)
officialReferences.covers: Says incentives for reviews must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says. Read in the CP-04 research on 2026-11-09.
